learning_outcomes.text: Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences
Students have developed the necessary learning skills to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy

Choose and apply the most appropriate methods and techniques to analyze and solve problems defined by data that represent a challenge due to their volume, velocity, variety, or heterogeneity, including computational, mathematical, statistical, and signal processing methods

Have the experimental and analytical skills to work autonomously, being able to propose experiments and to describe, analyze, evaluate, and interpret the resulting information to propose alternative and novel solutions to known and/or emerging problems
Create models and make decisions based on available data, combining acquired knowledge and being able to apply new knowledge to solve problems
Ability to integrate into a multidisciplinary team within the framework of a data science project
Ability to express data processing results clearly and convincingly, both in writing and orally
Understand computer architecture and identify and evaluate the performance and scalability of computer systems used for processing large volumes of data
Understand the basic properties of an infrastructure for data processing, storage, and transmission
Understand the architecture of the Internet network, its protocols, and the services it provides
Understand the connection of computers via local networks and their interconnection with other networks
Know the technologies and operation of peripherals for data storage and use systems for massive data storage
Know and use systems for massive data processing
Know, select, and use cloud components for data processing and storage

syllabus_topics: Introduction and historical evolution of networks

assessment_methods.method: Participation in online activities (Network Infrastructure questionnaire)
Participation in online activities (Computer Infrastructure questionnaire)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as: Note = NTeo x 0.45 + NPrac x 0.4 + NAsis x 0.05 + NAct x 0.1. A minimum grade of 40% is required in NTeo (theoretical part) and NPrac (practical part) to pass the course; otherwise, the final grade will be the lesser of 4.5 points and the calculated result. Attendance to at least 80% of in-person practical sessions is required for a positive attendance grade. In extraordinary calls and for differentiated evaluation, the final grade is Note = NTeo x 0.5 + NPrac x 0.5, with the same minimum grade requirement of 40% in NTeo and NPrac, and practical exam can only be taken if NTeo is above 40%.
